stem.text: The function g is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of g and its derivative are given in the table. Find \( \lim_{x \to 7} \left(3 g(x) - 8\right) \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The limit is -8, because g is differentiable at \( x = 7 \), so it is continuous there, and \( \lim_{x \to 7} g(x) = g(7) = 0 \).

worked_solution.text: g is differentiable at \( x = 7 \), so it is continuous there.
By the limit laws the limit is 3(0) - 8 = -8.
worked_solution.rule_named: sum and constant multiple limit laws

options.label: The limit is -8, because g is continuous at \( x = 7 \), so it is differentiable there, and \( \lim_{x \to 7} g(x) = g(7) = 0 \).
